profile.brand_role: Kimi is Moonshot AI's open frontier model family and agent product line, built for developers, coding agents, and knowledge workers who want open-source SOTA performance without closed-model pricing.

personality.note: Wins are celebrated with 'we'll keep our heads down and keep shipping' rather than hype superlatives; thanks the community constantly.
Single-emoji quote tweets (🤯, 🌘, 👀), jokes about 'hardwired into his prefrontal cortex', slippers for new hires.
Packs benchmark names, speedups, and architecture terms into bulleted highlights with exact numbers.
Apologizes transparently during capacity issues, humanizes the founder, says 'Happy coding!' to students.
Recurring framing: 'open intelligence should be instant, affordable, and borderless'; celebrates third parties building on its weights (Cursor).
'Keep building, keep shipping', 'Happy Shipping' used as sign-offs.

tone_scale.rationale: Casual emoji and jokes sit next to rigorous benchmark claims; bold on open-source SOTA but always softened with thanks and 'keep shipping'; deeply technical vocabulary (MoE, KV cache, prefill/decode) presented in plain, short sentences; consistently warm toward developers, partners, and students.

closing_patterns: 🔗 API / 🔗 Tech blog / 🔗 Weights & code link block

product_naming_rules: Kimi K3 / Kimi K2.6 / Kimi K2.5 (versioned, capital K, no space-hyphen in official posts)
Attention Residuals (with mathematical italic styling in titles)
Moonshot AI / Moonshot for the company
avoid: long unbroken paragraphs in launch posts
lexicon.numbers_style: Exact and dense: '2.8T MoE', '1M-token context', '300 parallel sub-agents × 4,000 steps', '1.72×–2.22× prefill speedup', '+21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2', '$0.16 / M tokens', '60-100 tok/s'. Benchmarks always named with scores in parentheses: 'SWE-bench Verified (76.8%)'.

formatting.bullets: Heavy use of 🔹 as the primary bullet; '-' hyphens in tutorials; '✅' for validated metrics; '>' used as sub-bullets for pricing/details.
formatting.emoji: Strategic, not decorative: 🔹 bullets, 🔗 for links, 🏆 for #1 rankings, 🎁/🎉 for promos, 🌘/🌙/🌖 moon imagery, 🤯/👀/🤗 as standalone reactions, ⚡️ for speed.
formatting.links: Nearly every substantive post ends with t.co links, often prefixed by '🔗' and labeled (API, Tech blog, Weights & code, GitHub, Details).
formatting.line_breaks: Generous: one idea per line, blank lines between sections, '-' used as a section divider in big launches.
formatting.mentions: Frequent @-mentions of partners (Fireworks, Baseten, Nebius, Modal, Databricks) and of @Kimi_Moonshot within quote tweets.

profile.claims_style: Claims are always anchored to named benchmarks and exact scores: 'Open-source SOTA on HLE w/ tools (54.0), SWE-Bench Pro (58.6)...' (2046249571882500354). Comparisons are scoped and hedged to 'open-source SOTA' or '#1 open model' rather than absolute #1, except on usage leaderboards (OpenRouter) where '#1 used model' is claimed with 'Real usage data doesn't lie. Developers are voting with their tokens.' (2018941851445997897). Competitor comparisons are rare and factual, e.g. 'only 20% the cost of Claude 4.5 Sonnet' (2016114773407236471). Speedups cite hardware and baseline: '1.72×–2.22× prefill speedup over the flash-linear-attention baseline on H20' (2081762799202746420).
profile.audience_address: Primarily developers and agent builders ('developers can start building', 'go build something amazing'), secondarily knowledge workers for Kimi Work tutorials (financial analysts, slide builders). Uses 'we/our' for Moonshot, 'you' for users, and never corporate third-person. Partners addressed warmly by name with public thanks.

reviewer_checklist: Does the post open with 'Introducing' / 'Meet' / 'X is now live' rather than a marketing hook?
Are capability claims tied to named benchmarks with exact scores or multipliers?
Is the strongest claim scoped as 'open-source SOTA' / '#1 open model' rather than unqualified 'best'?
Are specs written in the house style (2.8T, 1M-token context, tok/s, $X.XX / M tokens)?
Does the post use 🔹 bullets (not generic •) for highlights?
Does it end with the labeled 🔗 link block (API / Tech blog / Weights & code)?
Is availability stated plainly ('now live on ...') with a concrete date if weights are pending?
Is there a thank-you to developers, partners, or community where appropriate?
Is emoji use functional (🔹🔗🏆🌘) and limited — no decorative emoji strings?
Are hashtags absent (except event tags like #NVIDIAGTC)?
Does the post use 'we/our' for Moonshot and 'you' for the reader, with no first-person singular?
Is the tone warm but free of hype words like 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', or competitor-bashing?
profile.confidence_notes: Sample is English-only, so the Chinese-language voice (a major market for Moonshot) is unobservable. Reply/DM tone, crisis communications beyond one capacity incident, and long-form blog voice are out of scope. Quoted tweet texts are third-party content and were not used as voice evidence. Post-type labels were inferred from text. Dates appear to be from a future-dated scrape (2026); treat metrics as relative signals only.
